title: Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery — Credit for Recent Direct Payments in Waiver Measurement
content:
Direct payments a debtor has already made on a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** are credited against the expected repayment from which the amount a waiver request asks VA to waive is measured.

**Rule.** When two or more direct payments posted on the debt in the last six calendar months counted back from today, their whole total is credited. When exactly one did, 50 percent of it (the partial-credit percentage), rounded to the cent, is credited. Otherwise nothing is credited. The credit is subtracted from the monthly capacity multiplied by the horizon months counted, and what remains is the expected repayment.

**The six-month period.** A direct payment falls in the last six calendar months when fewer than six whole calendar months have passed from its posting date to today: on 20 October, a payment posted on 21 April falls in the period and one posted on 20 April does not. Benefit offsets are not direct payments and are not credited under this rule.

## Ledger illustrations (hypothetical)

| Direct payments posted in the period | Credit |
|---|---|
| 200.00 USD and 150.00 USD | 350.00 USD, the whole total |
| One payment of 312.46 USD | 50 percent of it, that is 156.23 USD |
| None (offsets only) | Nothing |

**Effect on the amount asked (hypothetical).** Where the monthly capacity multiplied by the horizon months counted is 600.00 USD and the credit is 350.00 USD, the expected repayment is 250.00 USD.
